title: A counterexample to Wall's D(2) problem
description: Wall's finite D(2) problem: is a finite complex of dimension three that looks two-dimensional to homology and cohomology with all coefficients homotopy equivalent to a finite complex of dimension two? Chain complexes twisted by a character of the fundamental group; Fox derivatives; an obstruction for complexes of dimension two proved by a tower of infinite cyclic covers; the finite plus construction; an explicit group that gives a counterexample. The new arguments are proved in full; of six standard theorems of algebraic topology, five are proved in the programme and the homotopy invariance of twisted homology is a named hypothesis. The course is an exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026).

units.title: Wall's D(2) problem and twisted homology

prerequisites: core course Algebraic Topology (D60): CW complexes, fundamental group, covering spaces, homology
groups, group rings and modules; tensor products over a ring

the standard theorems TOP1 to TOP6 of the first lesson: all proved in the programme (course cell-complexes-and-covering-spaces, lesson Frame fields and primary obstructions of the course on characteristic classes, core course Algebraic Topology) except the homotopy invariance in TOP5, a named hypothesis; everything else is proved in the four lessons
